text.p: Japanese car maker Toyota said on Friday that it is to launch a Baltic subsidiary to handle sales in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.
It said the sales target of the new company was 1,500 new cars this year and that its aim was to achieve annual sales of 5,000 units by the end of the century.
Toyota already has a company in Estonia, present since 1993, which handles the distribution and import of Toyota vehicles.
The new company will be formed by Sumitomo Corp and Toyota Finnish subsidiary Toyota Motor Finland Oy.
The new company will do the distribution and wholesale in Latvia and Lithuania, taking over from Sumitomo.

"Having seen these market areas stabilise and grow and having made good progress in Toyota Estonia, we decided to integrate the operations of these three countries into one distributor, Toyota Baltic AS," Toyota Baltic chairman Touri Ueno said in a statement.
The new company will handle distribution and wholesale and will have agreements with local dealers for retail.
Toyota currently has eight outlets in the Baltics, five in Estonia, two in Latvia and one in Lithuania.
